about: Text to the pieces read aloud one at a time. Input: paragraphs (already whitespace-collapsed and trimmed), language "en". Output: each piece's text, its paragraph's index, whether it starts that paragraph, and its [start, end) character offsets in the paragraph (UTF-16 code units).

cases.name: abbreviations don't end a sentence
paragraphs: Mr. Bennet replied that he had not. Dr. Smith, e.g. the third one, failed.

pieces.text: Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.
Dr. Smith, e.g. the third one, failed.

cases.name: an ellipsis on its own ends a sentence, one inside doesn't
paragraphs: Well, yes, but ... He left. I waited... and waited.

cases.name: a question in quotes followed by a capital is split (known limitation: "I asked" is read as its own sentence)
paragraphs: “Is that it?” I asked. She laughed.

cases.name: each paragraph starts a new piece
a sentence over 200 characters is cut after a semicolon
paragraphs: He walked for a long time through the forest, past the old temple where the priests had sung at dawn, past the river where the women washed their clothes and talked of the coming rains; then, as the sun went down behind the hills and the birds came home to the trees, he reached the edge of the city, tired and hungry and wondering whether anyone there would remember his name.

pieces.text: He walked for a long time through the forest, past the old temple where the priests had sung at dawn, past the river where the women washed their clothes and talked of the coming rains;
then, as the sun went down behind the hills and the birds came home to the trees, he reached the edge of the city, tired and hungry and wondering whether anyone there would remember his name.

cases.name: a sentence of 257 characters is cut after a comma (whole, it took Kokoro over 5 GB on a phone)
paragraphs: However little known the feelings or views of such a man may be on his first entering a neighbourhood, this truth is so well fixed in the minds of the surrounding families, that he is considered the rightful property of some one or other of their daughters.
